findings: MetricDetail nests each result under its metric name. Recall counts all rated relevant documents, including a relevant ID absent from the corpus; MRR uses a one-based first relevant position and -1 if none.

DCG discounts (2^rating-1)/log2(position+1). Normalization uses sorted rated documents limited by returned hit count. ERR uses stop probability (2^rating-1)/2^maximum_relevance and a continuing probability product. These arithmetic predictions need actual exact-binary replies.

TransportRankEvalAction forces metric k onto search size, fetches only summary_fields or disables _source, compiles templates once then renders request params. Parsing IO failures can enter the per-query failure map while another valid query proceeds. Other parser/runtime/template failures are not assumed equivalent.

RankEvalSpec.ScriptWithId parses default mustache scripts. RatedRequest rejects query plus template/params and params without template_id. Duplicate template IDs use Map.put so last source entry wins; this still requires native confirmation.

Exact JsonXContentParser converts EOF to XContentEOFException, whose parent XContentParseException extends IllegalArgumentException. Thus the selected malformed template output bypasses TransportRankEvalAction catch(IOException); expect a top-level400 even alongside a valid query. This is source-only until execution.

The public MRR name is MeanReciprocalRank.NAME=mean_reciprocal_rank, registered by RankEvalPlugin. Its ConstructingObjectParser diagnostic label reciprocal_rank is not an accepted metric name: the first retained native attempt established HTTP400 unknown field reciprocal_rank. This is a producer request-name mistake, not a server defect; retry uses the registered name.
